questions.scenario: A pull request changes an orders service template, and the reviewer runs `ansible-playbook deploy.yml --check --diff`. What evidence can a supported template task provide? The reviewer needs evidence about the proposed file content without changing a managed host.

options.text: A prediction of change plus the candidate content diff.
A guarantee that every handler will succeed.
A live mutation followed by automatic rollback.
A transaction across all managed hosts.

questions.explanation: Check mode predicts supported changes and diff mode shows supported before-and-after content without committing it. See [Ansible check and diff mode](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_checkmode.html).

questions.scenario: A playbook command task calls an external deployment API that cannot safely simulate its side effect. What is the safest behavior when the play runs in check mode? The pull-request job has no production mutation approval and must remain side-effect free.

options.text: Force `changed_when: true` during preview.
Gate it with `when: not ansible_check_mode` and validate it through another safe path.
Run it twice and compare the responses.
Ignore every error from the command.

questions.explanation: A task without a safe preview should be excluded from check mode and covered by separate validation. Inventing change output or ignoring failures misrepresents the evidence. See [Command module check-mode support](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/command_module.html#attributes).

questions.scenario: A production playbook is reusable across several inventories, and the operator wants to preview a canary change. Why should target inspection happen before the preview? The team wants to avoid producing a convincing preview for an accidentally broad host set.

options.text: Diff mode automatically expands host patterns.
Syntax check changes inventory membership.
A correct diff against the wrong hosts is still unsafe.
Check mode cannot use `--limit`.

questions.explanation: Scope and content are separate safety properties. Use `--list-hosts` or an equivalent inventory inspection to prove the target set before interpreting the proposed change. See [Ansible inventory patterns](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/inventory_guide/intro_patterns.html).

questions.scenario: An operator proves the production host set and completes a check-mode run without errors. Which limitation of that successful preview is still important? A protected real run is still waiting on approval and post-change verification.

options.text: The YAML definitely contains no variables.
Every module performed a real change.
The inventory contains exactly one host.
External side effects and post-change runtime health may still fail.

questions.explanation: Check mode is a simulation and support varies by module. It cannot guarantee runtime behavior after the real change. See [Check-mode limitations](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_checkmode.html).

questions.scenario: A template task specifies `validate: /usr/local/bin/orders --check-config %s` before writing the service file. What value does Ansible substitute for `%s`? The team wants invalid candidate content rejected before the destination file is replaced.

options.text: The current service status.
The path to the temporary candidate file validated before replacement.
The inventory hostname.
The Vault password source.

questions.explanation: The template module substitutes the temporary candidate path into the validation command and commits the destination only after validation succeeds. See [ansible.builtin.template](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/template_module.html).
